concerns.text: T005 (Logging Infrastructure) is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but explicitly states 'This task MUST follow T002c'. The [P] tag implies no dependency, yet the description enforces a strict sequential order. This is a semantic ordering violation: a task tagged [P] must be truly parallel-safe, not just 'runnable after' a specific gate.

T021b (Model Fitting) depends on T021a (VIF & Selection) to determine which predictor to drop. However, T021b is not marked as dependent on T021a in the task list structure (no explicit dependency marker or sequential ordering in the list). The 'Strict Order' note exists in the text but the task list itself presents them as a flat block, risking parallel execution by an automated runner.

T016c (FDR Correction) consumes the output of T016b (Raw Correlations). While the text notes 'Input: results/correlations.csv', the task list does not enforce the sequential dependency. If T016c runs before T016b completes, it will fail or read stale data. The [P] tag on T016c is incorrect as it has a hard data-flow dependency on T016b.

T024 (Validation for sufficient trials) states 'This task must run after T021a to ensure data integrity'. However, T024 is listed *after* T021c in the implementation block, and T021c (LRT & Output) depends on T021b which depends on T021a. T024 should logically precede T021b (fitting) to prevent fitting a model on insufficient data, but the current order places it after the model fitting logic has already been defined.

T002b (Setup Python 3.11 venv) is marked [P] but logically depends on T002a (Create requirements.txt) to have a file to install. While often done in parallel by humans, a deterministic runner needs T002a to exist before T002b can execute `pip install`. The [P] tag is semantically risky here.
